item.title: Grisaia: The Hundred Fruits of Gathering Opens Pre-Registration in Japan Ahead of a 2026 Release
item.description:
Grisaia: The Hundred Fruits of Gathering (Grisaia Shuuketsu no Hyakka), the new smartphone game in the Grisaia visual novel series, opened pre-registration in Japan on October 16, 2026 on the App Store and Google Play. Developer CLYRE plans to release it before the end of 2026.
It is a free-to-play character-raising simulation game with in-app purchases, and it brings together characters from across the series, from Grisaia no Kajitsu to Grisaia: Phantom Trigger, alongside six new girls created for this game.
Good Smile Company and Frontwing revealed the game on February 25, 2026, the day the series turned 15. The first entry, Grisaia no Kajitsu, came out on February 25, 2011, and the main trilogy follows Yuuji Kazami and the girls of Mihama Academy. CLYRE is in charge of development and will also run the game.
The official announcement of the Grisaia pre-registration came eight months after that reveal. Sign-ups go through the official store link, and the game needs iOS 15 or Android 9.0 and up.
The plot starts when six mysterious girls appear in front of Amane and the others, each claiming to be Yuuji Kazami’s daughter. They should be living 20 years in the future, yet they are somehow in the present. At the same time, a terrorist group calling itself the new Gaia Order declares war on government organizations including CIRS and SORD, led by a man named Heath Oslo whose silhouette looks very much like Yuuji.
Returning heroines include Yumiko Sakaki, Amane Suou, Michiru Matsushima, Makina Irisu, Sachi Komine and Kazuki Kazami, next to the six newcomers: Yuuma Sakaki, Yuuki Suou, Ichiru Matsushima, Serina Irisu, Yukiho Komine and Hifumi Kazami. Each one shares a family name with one of the original heroines.
The teaser released with the February reveal introduces the six girls and the new threat:
The game is built around raising each character and customizing her to your liking, winning battles for rewards and climbing the rankings. There is also a guild versus guild mode where players send their favorite girls into battle against other guilds.
The theme song is 「グレイズブレンダー」, sung by Yoshino Nanjo, with lyrics by Yuichi Kuwashima and music and arrangement by Jin Fujima of Elements Garden, the team behind earlier Grisaia songs. Its full music video is already out:
A separate visual novel set in the same story, Grisaia no Shinkajitsu -Shuuketsu no Hyakka-, is also in the works for 2027.

item.title: Monster Hunter Puzzles: Felyne Isles Ends Service on January 14, 2027, and an Offline Version Keeps Your Save
item.description:
Capcom has announced the end of service for Monster Hunter Puzzles: Felyne Isles, its match-3 puzzle game for iOS and Android. Online features go offline on January 14, 2027, and in-game purchases stop two months earlier, on November 12, 2026.
The game is not disappearing completely. On November 12 Capcom releases Monster Hunter Puzzles: Felyne Isles Furever, an offline version that players can move their current save into, and it will also come to Nintendo Switch and Steam.
The official end of service notice splits the closure into two steps:
Gems and boosters bought before the cutoff can still be used until January 14. After that date, the parts of the original app that do not need a connection keep working, but Capcom will no longer support it.
Felyne Isles Furever is a fully offline edition of the game. Progress carries over through each device’s cloud backup, iCloud on iOS and Google Cloud on Android, and Capcom will publish the step-by-step transfer guide closer to the date.
There are a few conditions to keep the save:
Capcom also warns that some features change in Furever, so part of the data will not carry over or will be converted. A connection is still needed at startup to confirm the content.
The Monster Hunter Puzzles shutdown closes a game that launched worldwide in June 2024. Players guide the Felynes through match-3 stages, push back monsters such as Rathalos, collect materials and spend them on outfits and on rebuilding their island.
The Switch and Steam versions of Furever do not have a release date yet. Capcom says it will share it later.

item.title: Love and Deepspace × Blade Runner 2049 Crossover Starts October 19 With Free Rewards
item.description:
Love and Deepspace starts its crossover with Blade Runner 2049 on October 19, 2026. Infold Games confirmed the collaboration on October 18 with a key visual of all five love interests, Xavier, Caleb, Rafayel, Sylus and Zayne, shown on giant neon screens over a rain-soaked city, and the tagline “Love is real. All for you.”
Blade Runner 2049 is Denis Villeneuve’s 2017 sequel to Ridley Scott’s Blade Runner, a story about replicants, memory and what makes a feeling real. The crossover leans on exactly that theme: the official announcement quotes the original film’s “tears in rain” line and frames the event around the question of whether love can be real.
Ahead of the launch, Infold released a concept trailer titled “Interlinked.”, a nod to the film’s baseline test. It opens on a wall of flickering CRT monitors, and Infold describes it as a story where memory, perception and every heartbeat lead to the same answer.
The crossover event is called Rendered Real and runs from 05:00 on October 19 to 04:59 on November 5 (server time). Checking in during the event gives three rewards for free:
Infold has said that the full event and reward details for Rendered Real will be shared in a separate announcement, so the rest of the Love and Deepspace Blade Runner content, including any limited banners, is still to be revealed. Everything above comes from the official crossover announcement on the game’s X account.
Love and Deepspace is a free-to-play 3D dating game with real-time combat, available on iOS, Android and PC. Players take the role of a Deepspace Hunter in the city of Linkon, fighting Wanderers alongside the five male leads, and the crossover brings that cast into Blade Runner’s world of replicants and rain.

item.title: Stella Sora Hits Steam on October 19 as Its 1st Anniversary Update Adds Firstlight Noya
item.description:
Stella Sora arrives on Steam on October 19, 2026, after that day’s maintenance (UTC-7), exactly one year after Yostar’s light-action RPG launched worldwide. The Stella Sora Steam release lands together with version 2.0, the 1st Anniversary update, which adds the limited ★5 Trekker Firstlight Noya, a new Main Story Special Chapter and 100 free limited recruitment tickets for logging in.
The game is free-to-play: a top-down action RPG where the player, the “Tyrant”, leads a team of Trekkers through labyrinths called Monoliths across the continent of Nova. The Steam page is already open for wishlists.
Firstlight Noya is a new ★5 Lux Trekker, recruitable in the limited banner At the First Piercing Light from October 19 to November 9, 2026. Her ★5 Runic Disc, My Guiding Star, runs in the parallel banner Resolve at the Tip of My Sword on the same dates. Her trailer presents her as a swordswoman who has kept fighting for a thousand years.
On top of that, the anniversary recruitment One Starlit Year, One Destined Reunion rewards pull milestones with Fated Reunion packs. New 3D outfits arrive in the shop for Shia and Firenze, while Noya gets a free 2D outfit just for logging in.
The Main Story Special Chapter, Wholeness at Reunion’s Dawn, stays permanently after the update, and its second half unlocks after October 29. The limited event of the same name runs until November 2, and its shop includes the ★5 Runic Disc Eternal Brilliance. Version 2.0 also adds The Tyrant’s Tower, a permanent system to customize your Monolith, collect treasures and spend time with the Trekkers, plus three limited modes: Speed & Wheels, Summit Show and Fatebound Stellar Deck. Every date is listed in Yostar’s version 2.0 notice.

item.title: Gundam Blitz Order Is the First Gundam Idle Game, and Its Network Test Sign-Ups Are Open
item.description:
Bandai Namco has announced Gundam Blitz Order, a new mobile game for iOS and Android, and opened sign-ups for the Gundam Blitz Order network test the same day. The test runs from November 18 to November 24, 2026, and applications close on October 26. There is no release date yet.
The game has official sites in Japanese, English, Korean and Traditional Chinese, and the test is not limited to Japan: players in the United States and England, South Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong can also apply.
The development team describes Gundam Blitz Order as the series’ first idle game: an RPG-style idle simulation where you collect mobile suits, power them up and build squads around each unit’s strengths. Mobile suits, warships and mobile armors from across the Mobile Suit Gundam franchise appear in the roster.
Play is split into two modes. In the idle mode, your squads fight on their own and gather upgrade materials over time, storing up to 24 hours of rewards, so one claim a day is enough to keep units growing. The more squads you unlock, the more you earn.
The active mode is where the strategy sits. Every unit belongs to one of six classes — Guardian, Striker, Assault, Artillery, Sniper and Support — and you pick both who deploys and where they stand on the field. The Gundam itself, for example, is a Guardian that soaks up hits for the team, while fragile Artillery units do best at the back, where some can pierce a whole line of enemies. Each unit also carries an EX Skill that charges over time and can be fired by hand or left on auto.
Beyond squad battles, the studio lists boss fights, warship escort missions where you protect a ship on its way to the goal, competitive content against other players, and side activities such as developing mobile suits and collecting items from the series. The announcement trailer shows the units in action:
The test version only includes part of the full game, with fewer units and modes than the final release, and maintenance is planned during the test. Places are drawn by lottery if applications exceed the cap, and selected players are notified by email on November 13.
Players outside Japan can apply through the official network test page, where each region’s terms list the residency and age requirements. News in English is posted on the game’s official X account, @g_blitz_order.
Gundam Blitz Order joins a Bandai Namco mobile line-up that already includes SD Gundam G Generation ETERNAL.

item.title: Tougen Anki: Crimson Inferno Opens Pre-Registration in Japan Ahead of a Global Rollout
item.description:
Com2uS Japan has opened pre-registration for Tougen Anki: Crimson Inferno, the first game based on the Tougen Anki TV anime. The turn-based RPG is coming to iOS, Android and PC, and everyone who signs up gets a ticket to pick an SSR character of their choice at launch.
Sign-ups opened on October 15, 2026 through the official pre-registration site, the Japanese App Store, Google Play and animate Games Online on PC. DMM GAMES and Google Play Games will open their own sign-ups later. There is no release date yet, and Com2uS says the game will expand to global regions after its Japanese launch.
Tougen Anki is Yura Urushibara’s manga in Akita Shoten’s Weekly Shonen Champion, with more than 6.5 million copies in print. It turns the Momotaro folk tale on its head: Shiki Ichinose learns he carries the blood of the Oni when the Momotaro Organization attacks him, and he enrolls at Rasetsu Academy to fight back.
The game retells the anime’s story in full 3D, with famous scenes from the series plus original episodes. The voice cast includes Kazuki Ura as Shiki and Hiroshi Kamiya as the instructor Naito Mudano.
Players collect characters from the series, build a team and pick skills for each fight. Combat is card-based: matching card marks and colors triggers enhanced attacks, and every character has an Inferno Skill, a flashy ultimate move that can turn a battle around.
The new trailer shows those skills in action, with Shiki, Jin Kougasaki, Tsubakiri Momomiya and Yomogi Momokusa fighting with their blood-based powers.
Beyond the SSR select ticket, the Tougen Anki Crimson Inferno pre-registration campaign unlocks more rewards as the sign-up count grows. Confirmed items include Crimson Stones, a [Rasetsu Academy] SR Select Ticket and 10 Standard Recruitment Tickets, all handed out after launch.
The PC version also has a Steam page, where the game is listed as coming soon.

item.title: Lord of Nazarick Will Shut Down on December 16, 2026, and Purchases Have Already Ended
item.description:
Lord of Nazarick, the turn-based RPG based on the OVERLORD anime, is shutting down. The team announced on October 14, 2026 that the servers will go offline on December 16, 2026, and purchases ended the same day as the announcement.
Because the closing schedule starts on the day it was announced, players have about two months left in the game and no way to buy anything in that time.
The official announcement splits the closure into two dates, both at 10:00 a.m. (UTC-2):
Players who already have the game installed can keep logging in until December 16.
The official Lord of Nazarick announcement
Just over two years of service The Lord of Nazarick shutdown comes just over two years after the game launched worldwide on October 29, 2024 on iOS and Android. Developed by Perfect World, it was published by Crunchyroll Games in the Americas, the UK, the Nordic countries and Oceania, and by A PLUS JAPAN in most of Europe and the Middle East.
The global release outlived the Chinese original, published by Bilibili Games, which shut down on December 29, 2025.

item.title: Millennium Tour ELF Is Out in Japan With 20 Summon Tickets and a Free 5-Star Gospel
item.description:
Millennium Tour ELF (千年の旅ELF) is out in Japan. ZeneXus opened the official service on October 14, 2026 on iOS and Android, and every pre-registration milestone was reached, so players who log in now collect 20 summon tickets and a 5-star Gospel.
The Japanese release goes ahead after the Chinese version stopped service, and the team behind it has promised that this one is built to last.
Pre-registration opened on August 7 and passed 500,000 sign-ups, the last step of the reward ladder. Each milestone adds summon tickets on top of upgrade materials:
The game is free to play with in-app purchases. Alongside the stores, ZeneXus opened a web shop on the official site where items cost 10% less when bought through the browser.
Millennium Tour ELF is a 3D turn-based RPG set in a world the gods have left behind. The player makes a pact with a witch and travels with the Gospels, the companions you collect. Battles are about pairing witches and Gospels and choosing skills. The Gospels are animated in Live2D and also appear as 3D models in combat.
The game is rated 12+ on the Japanese App Store and is also on Google Play. It is only available in Japan.
Millennium Tour has had a rough few years outside Japan. The Chinese original first shut down in February 2025 and later came back as a 2.0 version, and the English edition, Mirren: Star Legends, closed on March 31, 2026. With the Chinese service ending again, Japanese players asked whether their version would survive.
On October 12 the Japanese operations team answered in a statement. The game would launch on schedule, and the team says it is working closely with the developers with stable, long-term operation as its top priority. To back that up, it shared an early look at character designs that are still in development, with the warning that when and whether they reach the game is still undecided.
The official statement on the future of the Japanese version of Millennium Tour ELF
The official service then started on October 14, as planned.

item.title: Azur Promilia Sets an English Open Beta for Summer 2027 After 20 Million Pre-Registrations
item.description:
Manjuu, the studio behind Azur Lane, has announced that Azur Promilia will hold an English-version Open Beta Test in Summer 2027, on a dedicated U.S.-based server. It is the first time the game will be playable for English-speaking players, and the news comes as Azur Promilia passes 20 million pre-registrations worldwide.
The free-to-play fantasy world RPG is in development for PlayStation 5, PC, iOS and Android. There is still no global release date: the open beta window is the first firm step toward an English launch.
According to Manjuu’s official announcement, the Azur Promilia English open beta will run on its own server in the United States. The studio has not said yet which platforms the beta will cover or how players will sign up.
Alongside the date, Manjuu launched the game’s official English account on X, @AzurPromilia_EN, and released the first English promotional video, Kibo Safari. It tours the Kibo of Promilia, each with its own form and character:
— Azur Promilia (@AzurPromilia_EN) October 8, 2026
To celebrate the 20 million milestone, the account is also running a community giveaway whose top prize is a pair of Apple AirPods Max 2.
Azur Promilia is an open-world RPG built around creature companions called Kibo. They fight alongside you in combat and also help with the home system, taking on farming, crafting and material gathering. Some Kibo can be ridden, including winged ones that carry you across the map.
Until now, Azur Promilia had only been playable in tests in China, the latest being the Wayfare Test that began on September 17.
